item.title: Okayama Fruit Picking: White Peaches and Muscat — Guide
item.description: Because Okayama is Japan’s Fruit Kingdom, picking your own is one of the most enjoyable things to do here in season. Orchards in Akaiwa and the surrounding hills open from early summer for white peaches and from late summer into autumn for Muscat of Alexandria and Shine Muscat grapes. The usual format is a fixed-price session in the greenhouse or orchard, with an all-you-can-eat window of around 30 to 60 minutes, and the option to buy additional fruit to take away.

item.title: Tottori Pears: Nijisseiki and Farm Picking — Guide
item.description: The pear is Tottori’s proudest fruit, and the prefecture is the historic centre of the Nijisseiki or ‘20th-century’ pear — a round, pale-green, crisp and intensely juicy variety quite different from Western pears. Grown here for over a century, it made Tottori Japan’s leading pear producer, and the fruit remains a symbol of the prefecture. In late summer and autumn, orchards around Kurayoshi open for pear picking, letting visitors pick and eat their fill straight from the tree, and a dedicated pear museum in Kurayoshi tells the whole story with a giant pear-tree canopy inside.

item.title: Nagano Apple Picking & Cider Tasting: The Orchard Prefecture — Guide
item.description: Nagano is one of Japan’s leading apple-growing regions, its cool climate, sunny days and well-drained highland soil producing crisp, flavourful apples in varieties from Fuji to Shinano Gold, and each autumn its orchards open to visitors for apple picking. In a picking session, visitors harvest ripe apples straight from the tree, often with all-you-can-eat options, and many orchards and nearby producers also offer fresh apple juice and cider tasting, turning a simple harvest activity into a fuller taste of the region’s orchard culture.
